question: Who among the following is the hero of the Sanskrit historical poem, the 'Ramacharita' written by Sandhyakar Nandi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ramapala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ramacharita, written by the poet Sandhyakar Nandi in the 12th century CE, is a Sanskrit historical kavya (poem) whose hero is the Pala king Ramapala. (रामचरित — राजा रामपाल)

 

• The work is composed in a special dvyashraya (slesha) style, where every verse carries a double meaning — narrating simultaneously the story of Ramapala and the story of Rama from the Ramayana.

 

• It principally describes Ramapala's suppression of the Kaivarta rebellion in Varendra (North Bengal), led by Divya/Divvoka, and his subsequent recovery of the ancestral Pala kingdom.

 

• Ramapala was one of the last powerful rulers of the Pala dynasty, which ruled over Bengal and Bihar from the 8th to the 12th century CE.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pala dynasty was founded by Gopala in the mid-8th century CE and was a great patron of Buddhism, establishing institutions like Vikramashila and Odantapuri.

 

• Other Pala rulers of note include Dharmapala (founder of Vikramashila) and Devapala (who extended the empire to its greatest extent).

 

NOTE

 

• Gopala (Option 1): He was the founder of the Pala dynasty, not the hero of the Ramacharita.

 

• Devapala (Option 2): He was the most powerful Pala ruler who expanded the empire, but he is not the subject of this poem.

 

• Dharmapala (Option 4): He was the son of Gopala and a great patron of Buddhist learning, but he is not the hero of the Ramacharita.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, which group of Union Territories recorded the highest sex ratio?
option_1: Puducherry, Delhi, Andaman and Nicobar Islands
option_2: Puducherry, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puducherry, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, among the Union Territories, Puducherry recorded the highest sex ratio at 1,037 females per 1,000 males, followed by Lakshadweep (946) and Andaman and Nicobar Islands (878). (जनगणना 2011 — पुदुचेरी सर्वाधिक लिंगानुपात)

 

• India's overall sex ratio as per Census 2011 was 943 females per 1,000 males, the best figure since 1971.

 

• Among all states, Kerala had the highest sex ratio (1,084), while Daman and Diu had the lowest sex ratio among Union Territories (618), skewed by its migrant male workforce.

 

• The Chandigarh sex ratio (818) and Delhi sex ratio (866) are both lower than that of Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The child sex ratio (0-6 years) nationally fell to 919 in 2011, a matter of concern despite the improvement in the overall sex ratio.

 

• Haryana recorded the lowest sex ratio among all Indian states in Census 2011.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Puducherry, Delhi, A&N Islands): Incorrect — Delhi's sex ratio (866) is lower than Lakshadweep's (946), so Delhi should not be in this top group.

 

• Option 3 (Chandigarh, Puducherry, Lakshadweep): Incorrect — Chandigarh's sex ratio (818) is lower than that of Andaman and Nicobar Islands (878).

 

• Option 4 (Chandigarh, Puducherry, Delhi): Incorrect — both Chandigarh and Delhi have lower sex ratios than Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

question: Which of the following two quantities have the same dimensions?
option_4: Power and radius of circular motion
solution_text:
The correct answer is Work and torque.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Work is defined as Force × Displacement, and Torque is defined as Force × Perpendicular distance. Both therefore have the same dimensional formula: [ML²T⁻²]. (कार्य और बल आघूर्ण — समान विमा)

 

• Although Work (a scalar, measured in joules) and Torque (a vector, measured in newton-metres) represent physically different concepts, their dimensional formulas are identical because both are products of a force and a length.

 

• Moment of inertia has the dimension [ML²], and Power (work done per unit time) has the dimension [ML²T⁻³] — these are different from each other and from Work/Torque.

 

• Angular displacement is a dimensionless quantity (measured in radians), so it cannot share dimensions with Work [ML²T⁻²].

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other quantity pairs with identical dimensions include Impulse and Momentum [MLT⁻¹], and Pressure and Stress [ML⁻¹T⁻²].

 

• Energy, in all its forms (kinetic, potential, heat, etc.), always carries the dimension [ML²T⁻²], same as Work.

 

NOTE

 

• Power and moment of inertia (Option 2): Power is [ML²T⁻³] while moment of inertia is [ML²] — they are not the same.

 

• Work and angular displacement (Option 3): Work is [ML²T⁻²] while angular displacement is dimensionless — they are not the same.

 

• Power and radius of circular motion (Option 4): Power is [ML²T⁻³] while radius is simply a length, [L] — they are not the same.

question: The Doctrine of Lapse was an annexation policy devised by which of the following Governor-Generals of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Dalhousie.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Doctrine of Lapse was formulated and vigorously applied by Lord Dalhousie, Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856. (व्यपगत का सिद्धांत — लॉर्ड डलहौजी)

 

• Under this doctrine, any princely state ruled by a Hindu ruler who died without a natural male heir would be annexed by the British, disallowing adopted heirs from succeeding to the throne unless the adoption had prior British sanction.

 

• States annexed under this policy include Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853), and Nagpur (1854).

 

• The doctrine was deeply resented and is considered one of the major causes of discontent leading to the Revolt of 1857, especially in the case of Jhansi (Rani Lakshmibai) and Awadh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Dalhousie also introduced the railways, telegraph, and postal system in India and annexed Awadh (Oudh) in 1856 citing misgovernance (not under the Doctrine of Lapse, but the Doctrine of Misgovernance).

 

• The Doctrine of Lapse was formally abandoned after 1858, when the Crown took over administration of India from the East India Company.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Wellesley (Option 1): He is known for the Subsidiary Alliance system, not the Doctrine of Lapse.

 

• Lord Mayo (Option 3): He is known for founding the Rajkot and Mayo Colleges and for financial decentralisation; he was assassinated in the Andaman Islands in 1872.

 

• Lord Canning (Option 4): He was the last Governor-General and first Viceroy of India, during whose tenure the Revolt of 1857 occurred.

question: Which of the following is a man-made ecosystem?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aquarium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ecosystems are broadly classified into natural ecosystems (forming without human intervention) and artificial/man-made ecosystems (created and maintained by humans). An Aquarium is a classic example of a man-made ecosystem. (मानव निर्मित पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र — एक्वेरियम)

 

• A man-made ecosystem is deliberately constructed to sustain a chosen set of organisms in controlled conditions — other examples include crop fields, gardens, and aquaculture ponds.

 

• Desert, Forest, and Grassland are all natural terrestrial ecosystems that develop and sustain themselves without human design, shaped instead by climate, soil, and geography.

 

• Man-made ecosystems typically have lower biodiversity and simpler food chains than natural ecosystems because they are maintained for a specific human purpose.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Natural ecosystems are further divided into terrestrial ecosystems (forest, grassland, desert) and aquatic ecosystems (freshwater, marine).

 

• Other man-made ecosystems include orchards, terrariums, and urban parks.

 

NOTE

 

• Dessert (Option 2): As printed, this refers to the natural desert ecosystem, characterised by scanty rainfall and sparse vegetation — a natural, not man-made, ecosystem.

 

• Forest (Option 3): A naturally occurring ecosystem dominated by trees, formed over long periods without deliberate human construction.

 

• Grassland (Option 4): A naturally occurring ecosystem dominated by grasses, shaped by climate and grazing, not built by humans.

question: Who among the following famous Indian women cricketers announced retirement in June 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mithali Raj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mithali Raj, former captain of the Indian women's cricket team, announced her retirement from all forms of international cricket on 8 June 2022. (मिताली राज — सेवानिवृत्ति)

 

• Mithali Raj is the highest run-scorer in women's international (ODI) cricket and the first woman cricketer to score more than 7,000 runs in ODIs.

 

• She captained India to the finals of the ICC Women's World Cup in 2005 and 2017, and led India in the most number of international matches among Indian captains, male or female.

 

• She was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (2021), Padma Shri (2015), Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2015), and Arjuna Award (2003).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jhulan Goswami, India's legendary pace bowler and the highest wicket-taker in women's ODI cricket, retired from international cricket later, in September 2022.

 

• India's women's team achieved a historic Commonwealth Games 2022 silver medal in cricket shortly before Mithali Raj's retirement.

 

NOTE

 

• Smriti Mandhana (Option 1): She is an active top-order batter for India and had not retired in June 2022.

 

• Jhulan Goswami (Option 2): She retired from international cricket in September 2022, a few months after Mithali Raj.

 

• Anjum Chopra (Option 3): A former Indian captain and cricketer, she had already retired from international cricket in 2012, well before June 2022.

question: Which state government honoured Vani Jairam with the MS Subbulakshmi Award for 2019?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The MS Subbulakshmi Award, instituted in memory of the legendary Carnatic vocalist M.S. Subbulakshmi, is conferred by the Government of Tamil Nadu through its Tamil Nadu Eyal Isai Nataka Manram (Directorate of Art and Culture). (एम.एस. सुब्बुलक्ष्मी पुरस्कार — तमिलनाडु सरकार)

 

• Vani Jairam, a celebrated playback singer known for hits across Hindi, Tamil, and other Indian languages, was honoured with this state award.

 

• The award recognises outstanding lifetime contribution to music, echoing the legacy of M.S. Subbulakshmi, the first musician to be awarded the Bharat Ratna.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• M.S. Subbulakshmi was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1998, becoming the first musician to receive India's highest civilian honour.

 

• Vani Jairam is best known for playback songs like "Bole Re Papihara" (Guddi) and numerous Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Gujarati film songs.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 1): The MS Subbulakshmi Award is not a Maharashtra state honour.

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): Karnataka runs its own separate state film and cultural awards, not the MS Subbulakshmi Award.

 

• Odissa (Option 3): As printed (Odisha), this state has no connection to the MS Subbulakshmi Award, which is a Tamil Nadu state honour.

question: Which region in India receives less rainfall in summer, but heavy rainfall in winter season due to the retreating north easterly winds?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eastern coastal region.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Eastern coastal region of India (the Coromandel Coast, covering parts of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Odisha) receives comparatively little rainfall from the southwest monsoon but experiences heavy rainfall in October-December from the retreating/north-east monsoon. (पूर्वी तटीय क्षेत्र — शीतकालीन वर्षा)

 

• During the retreating monsoon (October-December) season, winds blow from land to sea (north-east to south-west), but they pick up moisture while crossing the Bay of Bengal and bring rainfall to the Tamil Nadu coast in particular.

 

• This is why Chennai and the Coromandel Coast receive their maximum annual rainfall in the winter months (October-December), unlike most of India, which gets its rainfall mainly from the southwest monsoon (June-September).

 

• The western coastal region, by contrast, receives very heavy rainfall during the southwest monsoon itself, due to the Western Ghats forcing moist air to rise.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The retreating monsoon is associated with the formation of tropical cyclones in the Bay of Bengal, which often make landfall on the eastern coast between October and December.

 

• Cherrapunji and Mawsynram in Meghalaya, though not coastal, receive India's highest rainfall due to orographic effects, mainly from the southwest monsoon.

 

NOTE

 

• Southern coastal region (Option 1): Rainfall pattern here varies by exact location but is not the classic example of retreating monsoon rain, unlike the south-eastern (Coromandel) coast.

 

• Western coastal region (Option 2): This region gets its heavy rainfall from the southwest (advancing) monsoon, not the retreating monsoon.

 

• Northern coastal region (Option 3): India's northern boundary is landlocked (Himalayan), so there is no "northern coastal region" receiving retreating-monsoon rainfall in this sense.

question:
Match the sports in List I with the sportsperson in List II who were in news for their sports achievement in 2022:

List I – Sports                         List II – Sportsman

A. Lakshya Sen                          i. Boxing

B. Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa             ii. Badminton

C. Nikhat Zareen                        iii. Shooting

D. Rudrankksh Patil                     iv. Chess
solution_text:
The correct answer is A-ii, B-iv, C-i, D-iii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lakshya Sen (A) is an Indian badminton (ii) player who won gold at the 2022 Commonwealth Games and silver at the 2022 BWF World Championships. (लक्ष्य सेन — बैडमिंटन)

 

• Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa (B) is a chess (iv) grandmaster who made headlines in 2022 by defeating world No. 1 Magnus Carlsen at the Airthings Masters.

 

• Nikhat Zareen (C) is an Indian boxer (i) who won the gold medal at the 2022 IBA Women's World Boxing Championships.

 

• Rudrankksh Patil (D) is an Indian shooter (iii) who won gold in the 10m air rifle event at the 2022 ISSF World Championship, becoming the youngest-ever world champion in the event.

 

• The correct matching is therefore A-ii (Badminton), B-iv (Chess), C-i (Boxing), D-iii (Shooting).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India had an outstanding sporting year in 2022, with achievements across chess, boxing, badminton, shooting, and the Commonwealth Games in Birmingham.

 

• Nikhat Zareen was later honoured with the Arjuna Award, and Rudrankksh Patil and Praggnanandhaa both received significant recognition for their achievements at a young age.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (A-iv, B-ii, C-i, D-iii): Incorrect — it wrongly pairs Lakshya Sen with Chess and Praggnanandhaa with Badminton.

 

• Option 2 (A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii): Incorrect — it wrongly pairs Lakshya Sen with Shooting and Rudrankksh Patil with Badminton.

 

• Option 3 (A-i, B-iv, C-ii, D-iii): Incorrect — it wrongly pairs Lakshya Sen with Boxing and Nikhat Zareen with Badminton.

question: Which of the following are the two basic categories of an ecosystem?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Terrestrial and Aquatic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ecosystems are broadly classified into two basic natural categories: the Terrestrial ecosystem (land-based) and the Aquatic ecosystem (water-based). (पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र — स्थलीय और जलीय)

 

• Terrestrial ecosystems include forests, grasslands, and deserts, while Aquatic ecosystems include freshwater ecosystems (rivers, lakes, ponds) and marine ecosystems (oceans, seas, estuaries).

 

• Forest, Lakes, Ponds, and Rivers listed in the other options are all specific *examples* within these two broader categories, not the two basic categories themselves.

 

• This classification forms the foundation of ecology, the branch of biology that studies the interaction of organisms with their environment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aquatic ecosystems are further divided into freshwater ecosystems (lentic — lakes/ponds, and lotic — rivers/streams) and marine ecosystems.

 

• Terrestrial ecosystems are further classified based on climate and vegetation into biomes such as tropical forest, temperate forest, tundra, and desert.

 

NOTE

 

• Forest and Aquatic (Option 1): Forest is only one type of terrestrial ecosystem, not the entire terrestrial category.

 

• Lakes and Ponds (Option 3): Both are specific types of freshwater (aquatic) ecosystems, not the two basic categories.

 

• Forest and Rivers (Option 4): Forest (terrestrial) and Rivers (aquatic) are individual examples, not the names of the two basic categories.

question: For which of the following states was the Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Orders (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022, introduced in the Parliament?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Orders (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022, was introduced in Parliament to include the Gond community as a Scheduled Tribe in four districts of Uttar Pradesh — Chitrakoot, Sonbhadra, Mirzapur, and Sant Ravidas Nagar. (अनुसूचित जनजाति संशोधन विधेयक — उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• The bill was passed during the Winter Session of Parliament, 2022, along with similar Constitution (SC/ST Orders) Amendment Bills for other states.

 

• Such bills amend the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 and the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, which list the castes/tribes recognised as SC/ST in each state.

 

• Similar, separately-titled amendment bills of 2022 covered changes for other states like Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Uttarakhand, but the specific Second Amendment Bill, 2022 referenced here pertains to Uttar Pradesh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of Tribal Affairs and Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment jointly pilot such SC/ST order amendment bills based on state government proposals and Registrar General of India recommendations.

 

• Inclusion in the ST list entitles the community to reservation benefits in education, employment, and legislature under Article 342 of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 1): A separate Constitution (SC/ST Orders) Amendment Bill, 2022 was introduced for Odisha, but it is not this particular Second Amendment Bill.

 

• Bihar (Option 2): No Second Amendment Bill, 2022 of this kind was introduced specifically for Bihar.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 4): No Second Amendment Bill, 2022 of this kind was introduced specifically for Madhya Pradesh.

question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution was borrowed from Irish Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Directive Principles of State Policy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), contained in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, were borrowed from the Irish Constitution (Constitution of the Irish Free State, 1937). (नीति निदेशक तत्व — आयरिश संविधान)

 

• DPSPs are non-justiciable guidelines directing the State to establish social and economic democracy, as envisioned by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, who called them "novel features" of the Indian Constitution.

 

• Ireland itself had borrowed the concept of Directive Principles from the Spanish Constitution, making it an indirect but well-documented borrowing.

 

• The method of election of the President of India was also borrowed from the Irish Constitution, but it is not one of the given options here.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fundamental Rights (Part III) were largely borrowed from the US Constitution.

 

• The Concurrent List was borrowed from the Australian Constitution, while the Rule of Law concept was borrowed from the British (UK) Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Concurrent List (Option 2): This feature was borrowed from the Australian Constitution, not the Irish Constitution.

 

• Fundamental Rights (Option 3): These were mainly inspired by the Bill of Rights of the US Constitution.

 

• Rule of Law (Option 4): This concept was borrowed from the British Constitution, not the Irish Constitution.

question: The Supreme Court of India comprises the Chief Justice and not more than ______ other Judges appointed by the President of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 33.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Article 124 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court of India comprises the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and, as amended by the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019, not more than 33 other judges. (उच्चतम न्यायालय — 33 अन्य न्यायाधीश)

 

• This makes the total sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court 34 judges (1 CJI + 33 other judges) at the time of this exam (September 2024).

 

• The strength of the Supreme Court has been increased periodically by Parliament through amendments — it started at 8 judges in 1950 (including the CJI) and has been raised several times since.

 

• Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President of India under the collegium system, following consultation as laid down in Constitution Bench judgments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The retirement age for a Supreme Court judge is 65 years, compared to 62 years for a High Court judge.

 

• Article 124 also lays down the eligibility criteria for appointment as a Supreme Court judge, including being a citizen of India and having specified judicial or legal experience.

 

NOTE

 

• 37 (Option 1):, 35 (Option 2):, and 38 (Option 3): These do not reflect the sanctioned strength of "other judges" (33) that was in effect as of this exam under the 2019 Amendment Act.

question: Ranjana Gauhar was awarded the Padma Shri Award (2003) for her contribution to which of the following Indian dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ranjana Gauhar is a renowned Indian classical dancer, choreographer, and writer who was awarded the Padma Shri in 2003 for her contribution to Odissi dance. (रंजना गौहर — ओडिसी नृत्य)

 

• She is also known for her contributions to Odissi and Mayurbhanj Chhau, and has served as the Chairperson of the Sahitya Kala Parishad, Delhi.

 

• Odissi is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating in the temples of Odisha, characterised by fluid torso movements (tribhangi) and depiction of Hindu mythology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's eight classical dance forms are: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), and Sattriya (Assam).

 

• Legendary Odissi exponents include Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sonal Mansingh, and Sanjukta Panigrahi.

 

NOTE

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 1): This classical dance form originates in Andhra Pradesh, not associated with Ranjana Gauhar's award.

 

• Sattriya (Option 2): This classical dance form originates in Assam, from the Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras).

 

• Manipuri (Option 4): This classical dance form originates in Manipur, known for its Raslila performances.

question: Who won the paralympic bronze medal in archery for India at Tokyo in 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harvinder Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Harvinder Singh won the bronze medal in the men's individual recurve open archery event at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, becoming the first Indian to win a Paralympic medal in archery. (हरविंदर सिंह — तीरंदाजी कांस्य पदक, टोक्यो पैरालंपिक)

 

• He defeated Mykhaylo Kokhan of Ukraine in the bronze medal match to achieve this historic feat.

 

• Harvinder Singh, from Ajitgarh, Punjab, later went on to win the gold medal in the same event at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, becoming India's first Paralympic gold medallist in archery.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's Tokyo 2020 Paralympics contingent won a record 19 medals (5 gold, 8 silver, 6 bronze), its best-ever performance at the time.

 

• Notable Indian Paralympic medallists at Tokyo 2020 include Avani Lekhara (shooting, gold), Sumit Antil (javelin, gold), and Krishna Nagar (badminton, gold).

 

NOTE

 

• Atanu Das (Option 1): An Indian able-bodied (Olympic, not Paralympic) archer; he did not win a Paralympic medal.

 

• Pravin Jadhav (Option 2): An Indian able-bodied Olympic archer who competed at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, not the Paralympics.

 

• Deepika Kumari (Option 3): A leading Indian able-bodied Olympic archer; she has not competed in or won a Paralympic medal.

question: Which of the following statements is correct about the composition of the agriculture sector and employment in GDP post-independence?
option_1: The proportion of employment has declined significantly but not the share of the agriculture sector in GDP.
option_2: The proportion of both the agriculture sector and employment in GDP has increased significantly.
option_3: The proportion of both the agriculture sector and employment in GDP has declined significantly.
option_4: The proportion of GDP contributed by the agricultural sector declined significantly but not the employment depending on the agriculture sector.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The proportion of GDP contributed by the agricultural sector declined significantly but not the employment depending on the agriculture sector.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Since independence, the share of agriculture in India's GDP has declined sharply — from around 50-55% in the early 1950s to less than 20% in recent decades. (कृषि क्षेत्र — जीडीपी हिस्सेदारी में गिरावट)

 

• However, the proportion of the workforce depending on agriculture has not declined proportionately — a large share of India's population (still over 40%) continues to depend on agriculture for livelihood.

 

• This mismatch — a shrinking GDP share but a still-large dependent workforce — reflects low productivity and disguised unemployment in the agricultural sector, and is a central concern of India's structural transformation debate.

 

• This trend indicates that while the services and industry sectors have grown much faster, labour has been slow to move out of agriculture into these higher-productivity sectors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• This phenomenon is often cited as evidence of a structural imbalance in the Indian economy, where GDP composition has "modernised" faster than employment composition.

 

• Government schemes like MGNREGA and rural non-farm employment initiatives aim to address underemployment linked to this imbalance.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Incorrect — it is the reverse of the true trend; employment dependence on agriculture has declined only modestly, not significantly, while GDP share has fallen sharply.

 

• Option 2: Incorrect — neither the GDP share nor the employment share of agriculture has increased since independence; both trends run counter to this.

 

• Option 3: Incorrect — while agriculture's GDP share has declined significantly, its employment share has declined only modestly, not significantly.

question: Which port is developed as a satellite port?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT), located at Nhava Sheva in Maharashtra, was developed as a satellite port to the Mumbai Port to relieve congestion at the older Mumbai (Bombay) harbour. (जवाहरलाल नेहरू बंदरगाह — मुंबई का उपग्रह बंदरगाह)

 

• Commissioned in 1989, JNPT is India's largest container port, handling a major share of the country's containerised cargo traffic.

 

• A satellite port is a smaller port built near a major/parent port specifically to absorb overflow traffic and ease congestion at the main port.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has 12 major ports, including Mumbai, JNPT, Kolkata (with Haldia as its subsidiary), Chennai, Cochin, Visakhapatnam, Kandla (Deendayal), Mormugao, New Mangalore, Paradip, Tuticorin (V.O. Chidambaranar), and Ennore (Kamarajar).

 

• Haldia Dock Complex functions as a subsidiary/satellite facility of the Kolkata (Syama Prasad Mookerjee) Port, similarly relieving pressure on the older port.

 

NOTE

 

• Mormugao (Option 1): Located in Goa, it primarily handles iron ore exports and is not classified as a satellite port.

 

• Haldia (Option 3): It functions as a subsidiary port to Kolkata Port (due to Kolkata's siltation issues), not to Mumbai.

 

• New Mangalore (Option 4): An independent major port in Karnataka, not developed as a satellite of another port.

question: Which polyatomic ionic compound is a white, crystalline powder used in fire extinguishers and to neutralise acids and bases?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sodium Bicarbonate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO₃), commonly known as baking soda, is a white crystalline polyatomic ionic compound used in fire extinguishers, as an antacid to neutralise stomach acid, and in baking. (सोडियम बाइकार्बोनेट — बेकिंग सोडा)

 

• In fire extinguishers (dry chemical/soda-acid type), sodium bicarbonate decomposes on heating to release carbon dioxide (CO₂), which smothers the fire by cutting off oxygen supply.

 

• Because it is a mild base, it is also used to neutralise excess stomach acid (as an antacid) and can neutralise mild acids in general chemistry applications.

 

• Its chemical formula, NaHCO₃, reflects its composition: a sodium cation (Na⁺) paired with the polyatomic bicarbonate anion (HCO₃⁻).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Heating sodium bicarbonate produces sodium carbonate (washing soda), water, and carbon dioxide: 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂.

 

• Sodium bicarbonate is manufactured industrially through the Solvay process.

 

NOTE

 

• Sodium Bisulphite (Option 1): Used mainly as a preservative and reducing/bleaching agent, not for fire extinguishing or acid-base neutralisation in this manner.

 

• Sodium Thiosulphate (Option 2): Used chiefly in photography (fixing agent) and as an antidote for cyanide poisoning, not in fire extinguishers.

 

• Sodium Chromate (Option 3): A yellow (not white) compound used as a corrosion inhibitor and in dyeing/leather tanning, not for fire extinguishing.

question: Chhath Puja is the main festival of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chhath Puja is the principal and most important festival of Bihar, also widely celebrated in eastern Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, and the Terai regions of Nepal. (छठ पूजा — बिहार)

 

• The festival is dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and Chhathi Maiya, and involves worshippers offering prayers while standing in water at sunset and sunrise.

 

• It is a four-day festival, typically falling in the Hindu month of Kartika (October-November), six days after Diwali, and is known for its rigorous fasting rituals without even water (Nirjala vrat).

 

• Chhath Puja is notable for having no idol worship and no priestly intermediary — the rituals are performed directly by devotees.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The four days of Chhath Puja are: Nahay Khay, Kharna, Sandhya Arghya (evening offering), and Usha Arghya (morning offering).

 

• Bihari and Purvanchali diaspora communities celebrate Chhath Puja globally, including in Mauritius, Trinidad, Fiji, and the Gulf countries.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 2): Its major festivals include Pongal and Tamil New Year, not Chhath Puja.

 

• Karnataka (Option 3): Its major festivals include Ugadi and Mysuru Dasara, not Chhath Puja.

 

• Assam (Option 4): Its major festivals include Bihu, not Chhath Puja.

question: Vindhyashakti was the founder of which of the following dynasties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vakataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vindhyashakti was the founder of the Vakataka dynasty, which rose to prominence in the Deccan region after the decline of the Satavahanas, around the mid-3rd century CE. (विंध्यशक्ति — वाकाटक वंश)

 

• The Vakatakas were a prominent Brahmin dynasty that ruled parts of central India and the Deccan, and were notable patrons of Sanskrit literature, art, and Hinduism.

 

• Vindhyashakti's successors, especially Pravarasena I, greatly expanded the kingdom, and later Vakataka rulers were connected by marriage to the imperial Guptas.

 

• The Vakatakas are also credited with patronising some of the later Buddhist cave paintings and sculptures at Ajanta, particularly during the reign of Harishena.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Prabhavatigupta, daughter of Chandragupta II, was married into the Vakataka royal family, reflecting close Gupta-Vakataka ties.

 

• The Vakataka period is considered a golden age for Deccan art, seen vividly in several caves at Ajanta.

 

NOTE

 

• Pallava (Option 1): This South Indian dynasty was founded by different rulers and is associated with Kanchipuram and Mahabalipuram, unrelated to Vindhyashakti.

 

• Maukhari (Option 2): This dynasty ruled in the Gangetic plains (Kannauj region) and was unrelated to Vindhyashakti.

 

• Chalukya (Option 4): This dynasty, founded later by Pulakeshin I, ruled from Badami/Vatapi, and is unrelated to Vindhyashakti.

question: Which Indian singer wrote 'Raag Sarita'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chintaman Raghunath Vyas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chintaman Raghunath Vyas (Pt. C.R. Vyas), a renowned Hindustani classical vocalist of the Gwalior-Bhendibazaar-Agra gharana blend, authored the book 'Raag Sarita', a compilation of bandishes (compositions) in various ragas. (राग सरिता — पंडित चिंतामणि रघुनाथ व्यास)

 

• 'Raag Sarita' is a well-known reference work used by students of Hindustani classical music for learning notated compositions across different ragas.

 

• Pt. C.R. Vyas was also honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contribution to Hindustani classical vocal music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pt. C.R. Vyas trained under gurus including Gajananbua Joshi and was known for blending multiple gharana styles into his own distinctive singing style.

 

• His son, Sanjeev Chimmalgi, is also a well-known Hindustani vocalist carrying forward his musical legacy.

 

NOTE

 

• Kesarbai Kerkar (Option 1): A legendary vocalist of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana, awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, but not the author of Raag Sarita.

 

• Balasaheb Poonchwale (Option 2): An Indian classical vocalist, but not associated with authoring Raag Sarita.

 

• Kumar Gandharva (Option 3): A highly acclaimed and innovative Hindustani classical vocalist, but not the author of Raag Sarita.

question: In which of the following areas did the Uprising of Khurda in 1817 take place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Uprising of Khurda (1817), also known as the Paika Rebellion, took place in the Khurda region of Odisha, led by the traditional militia known as the Paikas, under the leadership of Bakshi Jagabandhu. (खुरदा विद्रोह (पाइक विद्रोह) — ओडिशा)

 

• The Paikas, hereditary land-owning militia of the Gajapati kings of Odisha, revolted against the British after being stripped of their rent-free land grants (Nish-kar Jagirs) following the British annexation of Khurda in 1803.

 

• The revolt is often regarded by historians as an early and significant precursor to the 1857 Revolt, reflecting widespread discontent against British agrarian and land-revenue policies.

 

• The rebellion was ultimately suppressed by 1818, though Bakshi Jagabandhu continued resistance until his eventual surrender in 1825.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Government of India officially recognised the Paika Rebellion of 1817 as a significant freedom struggle event during its bicentenary commemorations in 2017.

 

• Odisha was under British control from the early 19th century onward, following the Anglo-Maratha Wars.

 

NOTE

 

• United Province (Option 1): This region (present-day Uttar Pradesh) was the site of later uprisings including parts of the 1857 revolt, not the Khurda Uprising.

 

• Madras (Option 3): The Khurda Uprising did not take place in the Madras Presidency.

 

• Bengal (Option 4): Though administratively close to Odisha at various points, the Khurda Uprising is specifically located within Odisha, not Bengal proper.

question: The central bank of India or Reserve Bank of India was created before Independence, in the year 1934. The recommendation to create a central bank was made by a commission called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hilton Young Commission.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hilton Young Commission (formally, the Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, 1926) recommended the establishment of a central bank for India, leading to the enactment of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 and the RBI commencing operations in 1935. (हिल्टन यंग आयोग — भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक की सिफारिश)

 

• The commission was headed by Edward Hilton Young and was tasked with examining India's currency and exchange administration.

 

• The RBI Act, 1934 was passed based on this commission's recommendations, and the Reserve Bank of India began functioning on 1 April 1935, initially as a privately owned institution before being nationalised in 1949.

 

• The Hilton Young Commission also recommended the gold-exchange standard for India's currency system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first Governor of the RBI was Sir Osborne Smith, and the first Indian Governor was C.D. Deshmukh.

 

• The RBI's head office moved from Kolkata to Mumbai in 1937.

 

NOTE

 

• Dr. Raja Chelliah Committee (Option 1): This committee (1991) is associated with tax reforms in India, not the creation of RBI.

 

• Kothari Commission (Option 2): This commission (1964-66) is associated with education policy reforms in India, not the creation of RBI.

 

• Narasimham Committee (Option 3): This committee (1991 and 1998) is associated with banking sector reforms, not the creation of the RBI itself.

question: Sundari trees are found in which type of forests in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mangrove forests.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sundari trees (Heritiera fomes) are found predominantly in the mangrove forests of the Sundarbans delta (West Bengal), which is in fact named after this very tree. (सुंदरी वृक्ष — मैंग्रोव वन, सुंदरबन)

 

• Mangrove forests grow in the tidal, saline, waterlogged deltaic regions along India's coast, especially at the mouths of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta.

 

• Sundari wood is valued for boat-building and construction due to its durability and resistance to decay, though overexploitation and rising salinity threaten the species today.

 

• The Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove forest and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, also famous for being home to the Royal Bengal Tiger.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important mangrove regions in India include the Bhitarkanika mangroves (Odisha) and the Godavari-Krishna delta mangroves (Andhra Pradesh).

 

• Mangrove ecosystems play a crucial role as breeding grounds for fish and as natural barriers against coastal erosion and cyclones.

 

NOTE

 

• Tropical deciduous forests (Option 2): These forests (e.g., teel/sal-dominated) shed their leaves in a particular season and are not associated with the Sundari tree.

 

• The thorn forests and scrubs (Option 3): These are found in arid/semi-arid regions like Rajasthan, entirely unsuited to the Sundari tree's saline, waterlogged habitat.

 

• Tropical evergreen forests (Option 4): These dense, non-seasonal forests (e.g., Western Ghats, Northeast India) are a different ecosystem from the saline mangrove habitat of the Sundari tree.

question: Which team won the T20 cricket event, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy 2022-2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mumbai won the 2022-23 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, India's premier domestic T20 tournament, by beating Himachal Pradesh by four wickets in the final. (मुंबई — सैयद मुश्ताक अली ट्रॉफी 2022-23 विजेता)

 

• This was Mumbai's first-ever Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy title, achieved by chasing down Himachal Pradesh's total in the final held in November 2022.

 

• Shreyas Iyer captained the Mumbai side to this title, with strong contributions from several key batters through the tournament.

 

• The Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy is named after the legendary former Indian cricketer Syed Mushtaq Ali, regarded as India's first great T20-style attacking batsman of the pre-independence era.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vidarbha, one of the other listed teams, was defeated by Mumbai in the semi-final of the 2022-23 tournament (with a memorable innings from Shreyas Iyer).

 

• Mumbai went on to also win subsequent editions of the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy in later years, cementing its dominance in the tournament.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 2): Punjab did not win the 2022-23 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy.

 

• Vidarbha (Option 3): Vidarbha was defeated by Mumbai in the semi-final of the 2022-23 edition, so they did not win the title.

 

• Himanchal Pradesh (Option 4): As printed (Himachal Pradesh), this team was the runner-up, losing to Mumbai in the final, not the winner.
